llmResponse.agendaChanges: Item 9.2 (First Reading and Discussion of Board Policy 4154/4254/4354 - Health and Welfare Benefits) was pulled from the agenda by Trustee MacAvoy on behalf of the board policy committee for further revisions. Item 9.1 was modified to cover only Adelante Selby SPSA, as the Orion SPSA presentation was pulled due to presenter Ms. Rivera having a family emergency. The board noted Orion parents could speak during oral communication. Section 2 Welcome was delivered by President Márquez (not Vice President Lawson as listed). The agenda was otherwise followed in order.

items.title: Report out on Closed Session from January 20, 2023

publicComments.name: Peter Cohen
publicComments.summary: Thanked district staff for correcting enrollment issues and advocated for expanding Mandarin immersion and TK programs to align with California's 2030 bilingual education goals.

publicComments.name: Alexis Betts
publicComments.summary: Asked the board to accommodate all families wanting to enroll in the Mandarin Immersion program to ensure a healthy, sustainable program through eighth grade.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly
publicComments.summary: Advocated for underserved families in the MI program, requested a different school structure to better serve both programs, and urged the district to apply for the TCLP program for additional teacher support.

publicComments.name: William Dennis
publicComments.summary: Expressed support for sibling priority in the Mandarin Immersion program so his younger daughter could attend the same school as his son.

publicComments.name: Deepika Germany (speaker was husband)
publicComments.summary: Advocated for an additional TK class in the Mandarin Immersion program, noting his daughter is currently on the waitlist.

publicComments.name: Tina Chung
publicComments.summary: Advocated for additional Mandarin Immersion TK classes to benefit more students, including her son who knows some Mandarin.

publicComments.name: Ronnie Le
publicComments.summary: Advocated for continuing and expanding the Mandarin Immersion program, citing high academic performance data and the importance of bilingual education for her incoming kindergartener.

publicComments.name: Jackie Chen
publicComments.summary: Described the stressful waitlist experience for the MI program and requested two TK MI classes and three kindergarten MI classes.

publicComments.name: Julia Selesneva
publicComments.summary: Praised the academic rigor of the Mandarin Immersion program and advocated for expanding kindergarten and TK enrollment.

publicComments.name: Alex (last name not given)
publicComments.summary: Supported expansion of the Mandarin Immersion TK and kindergarten programs, connecting early bilingual immersion to values like open-mindedness and empathy.

publicComments.name: Angela Kang
publicComments.summary: Advocated for additional MI TK classes so that all interested families, including hers, could have the opportunity to enroll their children.

publicComments.name: Sam Christensen
publicComments.summary: Stated that the Mandarin Immersion program is the only school option his family is interested in and expressed support for expanding the TK program.

publicComments.name: Chris Terry
publicComments.summary: Raised concerns about fairness in the MI lottery, specifically the Odyssey Preschool preference and TK sibling preference crowding out other kindergarten applicants, and asked the board to reform the lottery or add more classes.

publicComments.name: Jasper Chen
publicComments.summary: Thanked the board for building a great community and encouraged investment in and expansion of the Mandarin Immersion program.

publicComments.name: Anna Lee Moraz
publicComments.summary: A Spanish-speaking parent from Mexico raised concerns about accessibility of the MI program for low-income families, including the cost of after-school programs.

publicComments.name: Keith Simmons
publicComments.summary: Requested expansion of sibling priority to TK, two TK MI classes, three kindergarten MI classes, and urged the board to examine the Adelante program's waitlist given the importance of early language acquisition.

publicComments.name: Heather Stamper
publicComments.summary: Supported expanding TK and kindergarten MI classes to stabilize enrollment and prevent attrition that weakens the program in upper grades.

publicComments.name: Mele Rosallo
publicComments.summary: Advocated for more funding and support resources for MI students with learning disabilities, including a Mandarin resource teacher and additional TK access.

publicComments.name: Richard Pont
publicComments.summary: Shared his family's positive experience with the MI program and requested expansion so other families with children, including those with IEPs, can participate.

publicComments.name: Micah Bonara
publicComments.summary: Shared relief that his twin boys got off the MI waitlist and supported expansion of the TK and kindergarten MI programs to spare families the emotional stress of the waitlist process.

publicComments.name: Sarah Rutherford
publicComments.summary: Asked for consistency in the sibling priority policy between TK and other grades, especially in light of Universal TK expansion.

publicComments.name: Tiffany Chao Bev
publicComments.summary: Stated that the Mandarin Immersion program was a reason her family moved to Redwood City and urged expansion of TK and kindergarten MI classes.

publicComments.name: Xiang Yen
publicComments.summary: Asked how the community could help move forward MI program expansion, offering to write letters or take other actions as guided by the board.

publicComments.name: Julia Feng
publicComments.summary: Questioned whether the district should artificially cap demand for the MI program and emphasized the narrow TK/kindergarten enrollment window for immersion learners.

publicComments.name: Doshi (first name not given)
publicComments.summary: Advocated for adding an MI TK class, noting her daughter is on the waitlist and that out-of-district families are also seeking to enroll, making competition even harder for in-district residents.

publicComments.name: Philip Guy
publicComments.summary: Thanked the district for the MI program and asked the board to expand it as much as possible, offering community support to help make that happen.

publicComments.name: Olanes Villanueva (interpreted)
publicComments.summary: A Spanish-speaking parent with three children in the MI program asked for more support for Latino families in the program, including in-school tutoring services so children are not left behind.

publicComments.name: Ileana Harrison
publicComments.summary: Thanked Dr. Baker for recognizing MI performers at the Lunar New Year fair and requested two TK MI classes and three kindergarten MI classes.

publicComments.name: Kyle Zipes
publicComments.summary: Argued that a lottery for school placement is unacceptable and urged the board to accommodate all MI-interested families, suggesting a dedicated campus if needed.
